rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING HUMAN CLONING IN THE PHILIPPINES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is the policy of the State to value the dignity of every human person and guarantee full respect for human rights. The State recognizes the sanctity of family life, and is committed to protect and strengthen the family as a basic autonomous social institution. Towards this end, the government must and shall ban the conduct of human cloning since very human being has intrinsic dignity and worth which must be preserved, respected and safeguarded. It shall be unlawful to conduct orundertake human cloning in the Philippines, even on an experimental basis.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF PSYCHOLOGY, CREATING FOR THIS PURPOSE A PSYCHOLOGY BOARD, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Institutions and organizations have recognized the vital role of psychology. As a result, corporations and government institutions are now able to create programs that address stress and other hazards in the workplace. Schools and other institutions of learning are able to put into place counseling programs that enhance the learner's intellectual and emotional stability. Penal institutions likewise are able to draw on psychology's vast resources in order to prepare inmates for theireventual reintegration into society. Yet for all its significance and advances, psychology has remained unregulated.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05992

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AND VESTING IN IT THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY OF ENFORCING MARITIME SAFETY RULES AND REGULATIONS AS WELL AS ANY OTHER MATTER RELATED TO THE PERFORMANCE OF SAFETY OF LIFE AND PROPERTY FUNCTION WITHIN PHILIPPINE TERRITORIAL WATERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed measure seeks to confer upon the Philippine Coast Guard the primary responsibility of overseeing the safety of life and property at sea of all seafarers.  It intends to resolve the confusion that arises in the aftermath of sea disasters where government agencies usually point at each other as being negligent or responsible for the sea mishaps.  It does so by delineating the functions of the government agencies involved in the protection of seafarers, sea cargo, and vessels.  It tasks the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) with the duty of issuing rules, regulations and standards pertaining to the maritime industry, safety and other related matters while the Philippine Coast Guard is tasked with the duty of enforcing and impplementing such rules, regulations and standards promulgated by the MARINA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE LIABILITIES OF INDIRECT EMPLOYERS IN JOB CONTRACTING, COVERING OTHER BENEFITS DUE THEIR EMPLOYEES, FOR THIS PURPOSE, AMENDING ARTICLE 106 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: IN THE EVENT THAT THE EMPLOYEES OF THE CONTRACTOR OF SUBCONTRACTOR HAVE RENDERED AT LEAST ONE YEAR OF SERVICE TO THE SAME EMPLOYER, WHETHER OR NOT SUCH EMPLOYMENT IS CONTINUOUS, SUCH EMPLOYER SHALL ALSO BE JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY BE LIABLE WITH THE CONTRACTOR OR SUBCONTRACTOR FOR THE PAYMENT OF THE EMPLOYEES' BENEFITS, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO THEIR SEPARATION OR RETIREMENT BENEFITS, PROVIDED, THAT THE LIABILITY OF THE INDIRECT EMPLOYER SHALL BE LIMITED ONLY TO THE PERIOD THAT SUCH EMPLOYEERENDERED SERVICES TO THE SAID INDIRECT EMPLOYER, THE AVAILMENT AND GRANT OF SEPARATION, RETIREMENT AND OTHER BENEFITS SHALL BE IN ACCORDANCE WITH EXISTING LAWS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FUND AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Science and Technology have been recognized as the engines of growth for national development and progress. In recognition of the crucial role of science and technology in the country's drive for NIChood status the 1987 Constitution accords strong support for the development of this sector. The proceeds of the Science and Technology Fund shall be specifically utilized for capital outlays which are aimed at the realization of the following S & T thrusts: (1) Human Resource Development(HRD); (2) Institution development through upgrading of research laboratories; (3) Accelerating research and development (R&D); (4) Intensification of information and communication program and infrastructure; and (5) Enhancement of technology transffer and other technical services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE TRANSFER OF OFFENDERS TO OR FROM FOREIGN COUNTRIES
rows.abstract: "Transfer of Prisoners Act of 2001." This Act shall only be applicable to the transfer of an offender to and from a foreign country pursuant to a treaty that is in force: Provided, That a sentence imposed by a foreign court upon an offender who is subsequently transferred to the Philippines pursuant to a treaty shall be fully executed in the Philippines even though the treaty under which the offender was transferred is no longer in force.  An offender may be transferred from the Philippines toa country of which the offender is a citizen or national. Only an offender who is a Filipino citizen may be transferred to the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE ROLE OF THE VERNACULAR AND FILIPINO IN FUNCTIONAL LITERACY AND PROVIDING GUIDELINES FOR ITS CLASSROOM USE
rows.abstract: In Grades One, Two, and Three of the elementary level, the vernacular shall be the language of instruction for all subjects with Filipino as a separate subject and the auxiliary language of instruction. Filipino shall continue to be taught as a separate subject until the fourth year of secondary education.  In Grade Three, English as a foreign language shall be introduced as a separate subject and shall continue to be taught as a separate subject until the fourth year of secondary education.  In Grade Four, Filipino shall be the language of instruction and shall continue to be the language of instruction for all subjects, except English, until the fourth year of secondary education.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to lay emphasis on the ensuring of equal employment opportunities for all citizen of the Philippines and eliminate the too liberal provisions allowed in other countries relative to accomodating people of varying political options, race, national origin, and the like, which the Philippines is still obviously unprepared to handle. Said bill addresses these concerns:  - equal access to information on job vacancies - equal opportunity to be hired - objective evaluation of qualifications for specific job requirements - equal pay for work of equal value - equal access to training/schola rships - equal access to promotion - equal access to merit increases and other benefits - objective job performance evaluation/asse ssment
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-30

rows.abstract: "Gender Equality in the Educational System." Rationale: It is hereby declared the policy of the State to promote the equality of men and women through the elimination of stereotyping of the roles of both sexes in our social and cultural norms. Pursuant thereto, the State shall provide gender equality in the educational system.  The Department of Education, Culture and Sports shall be responsible primarily for examining all the curricula and learning materials with a view to removing sex-bias and to develop non-sexist resources and curricular materials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-30

rows.author: B001
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09163) enacted on 2002-01-23
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL SERVICE TRAINING PROGRAM AS A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE RESERVED OFFICERS' TRAINING CORPS PROGRAM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 1, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `NATIONAL DEFENSE ACT', AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7077, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `CITIZEN ARMED FORCE OR THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES RESERVIST ACT', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill envisions to achieve these objectives: a. To provide college students an alternative to military training as a requirement for graduation in a baccaulaureate degree; and b. To ensure that the country will ahve enough reservists to meet theminimum yearly requirement for the Armed Forces of the Philippines' reserve force development.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03593

rows.author: B001
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09163) enacted on 2002-01-23
rows.title_full: AN ACT SUSPENDING THE OPERATION OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7077, ENTITLED `CITIZEN ARMED FORCE OR ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES RESERVISTS ACT', WITH RESPECT TO THE PROVISIONS ON THE RESERVE OFFICERS' TRAINING CORPS PROGRAM FOR THE SCHOOL YEARS 2001-2002, 2002-2003 AND 2003-2004
rows.abstract: The operation of Republic Act No. 7077 with respect to the provisions on Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) program is suspended for the School Years 2001-2002, 2002-2003, and 2003-2004. All students who are graduating in any Baccaulaureate degree on October 2001 until March 2004 are hereby exempted from taking the ROTC: Provided, That after the lifting of the suspension, students who have only three (3) semesters or less left remaining in their academic subjects before their graduation shall undergo the program corresponding to the aforesaid number of remaining semester or semesters.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03593

first_reading.comm_act: change of ctte. ref'l from Revision of Laws as per J.21;p.20( dtd. Sept. 5,2001)

rows.author: C013
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING THE ROLE OF THE COOPERATIVE MOVEMENT IN COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT, STRENGTHENING AND DEFINING THE REGULATORY AND ADJUDICATIVE FUNCTIONS OF THE COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (CDA), RENAMING IT AS THE COOPERATIVE REGULATORY AND DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (CRDA) AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES, AMENDING THEREFOR REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-NINE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill calls to amend the Charter of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) as embodied in Republic Act 6939, in order to strengthen the agency's regulatory and/or supervisory powers, modufy its developmental functions, and provide it with quasi-judicial powers.  It is envisioned that the streamlining of the CDA will put the agency in a better position not only to ensure discipline within the burgeoning cooperative sector, but help facilitate the growth of quality cooperatives by allowing the cooperative movement itself to handle institutional development of cooperatives nationwide.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C013
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING THE STATE SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM AND FOR THIS PURPOSE REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED FORTY HUNDRED AND NINETY
rows.abstract: There is hereby established a State Scholarship Program, hereinafter referred to as the Program, which shall be open to poor but deserving students who shall be selected annually from the graduating classes of all public and private high schools throughout the Philippines. Qualified students for the Program shall be granted scholarships and whose expenses, like tuition, matriculation, and other school fees, prescribed textbooks and equipment, board and lodging, clothing, travelling expenses, and miscellaneous allowances, shall be defrayed from the funds appropriated by law or contributed from other sources for the Program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C013
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-07-30, transmitted to on 2002-08-05 and received by the Senate on 2002-08-05
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE EDUCATION AND LICENSURE OF PHYSICIANS AND THE PRACTICE OF MEDICINE IN THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 2382, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Philippine Medical Act of 2001."  The purpose of this bill is to update and revitalize the 40-year old Medical Act of the Philippines and, as a result, provide a law that is more responsive to new medical developments and ever-changing requirementsof our developing society. Primary changes include provisions to promote continuing medical education among doctors. The erstwhile Department of Education and Board of Medical Examiners are to be changed to Commission on Higer Education (CHED) and Board of Medicine, respectively. Likewise, the composition of the Board of Medical Education is to be expanded. Subjects in the medical course are also increased.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04729

rows.author: C013
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09292) enacted on 2004-04-17
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MORE RESPONSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE REGULATION FOR THE REGISTRATION, LICENSING AND PRACTICE OF ELECTRONICS ENGINEERS AND ELECTRONICS TECHNICIANS, REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5734 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The State recognizes the importance of electronics engineering in nation building and development. The State shall therefore develop and nurture competent, virtuous, productive, and wellrounded Professional Electronic Engineers, Electronic Engineers and Electronic Technicians whose standards of practice and service shall be excellent, qualitative, world-class and globally competitive through inviolable, honest, effective and credible licensure examinations and through regulatory measures, programs and activities that foster their continuing professional education.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05224

rows.author: C013
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-29, transmitted to on 2002-12-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-12-04
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE COOPERATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-NINE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-EIGHT
rows.abstract: Since its inception, the cooperative movement has aimed to uplift the standards of living of the people especially the low income sectors. However, it is to be observed that the growth and development of cooperatives remain slow. The law may not beattractive enough to encourage some groups to organize into a cooperative. Thus, in order to optimize the efficiency and effectiveness of the Cooperative Code of the Philippines, pursuant to the Constitutional provision calling for the promotion anddevelopment of cooperatives to help attain economic development and social justice, this measure is being proposed.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05206

rows.status: Substituted by HB04965

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING THE USE OF CELLULAR PHONES IN AIRPLANES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The use of cellular phones while on board airplanes is dangerous. Cellular phones emit electro-magneti c frequencies which interfere, alter or jam computer programmed precision instruments. They also are known to jam communication instruments. In fact, the manufacturers of cellular phones themselves have inidcated in the manual that comes with every purchase of a cellular phone that such device is not to be used in certain conditions because of the inherent dangers it poses. However,not all consumers of this product read and follow such safety tips included in the manual which leads to accidents or disasters.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: D062
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09257) enacted on 2004-03-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES ON PHARMACIES AND DRUG STORES WHICH REFUSE TO HONOR SENIOR CITIZENS CARD ISSUED BY THE GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract: In addition to the appropriate penalties provided under Republic Act No. 7432, the owner, manager and/or employee of any pharmacy and drug store who refuses to honor the senior citizen card issued by the government shall, if found guilty, be punished with a fine of not less than One Thousand Pesos (P1,000) nor more than Five Thousand Pesos or imprisonment of not less than one (1) month nor more than six (6) months or both such fine and imprisonment at the discretion of the court.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05987

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CHAPTER 2, TITLE V OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: NOTWITHSTANDING ANY LAW TO THE CONTRARY, THE FAMILY HOME, WHILE REMAINING AS SUCH, SHALL LIKEWISE BE EXEMPTION FROM THE PAYMENTF REAL PROPERTY TAX OR ANY OTHER TAX ON REAL PROPERTY.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RATIONALIZE THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF ALL LAWS ON OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH STANDARDS AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to identify the lead agency which will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing the activities of all agencies that are involved in the promotion of occupational safety and health standards and environmental protection programs. It also seeks to authorize the lead agency, after consultations with participating agencies and sectors concerned, to prescribe administrative fines in cases of violations of such standards and regulations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM INCOME TAXATION THE INITIAL THREE (3) YEARS SALARY OF SCHOOL TEACHERS, BOTH IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY
rows.abstract: It is necessary that certain incentives be given by government to new teacher during their first three years of services. Giving exemptions from payment of income tax during the first three years of employment could be added incentives that will notonly help solve the problem of teacher shortage but also improve the quality of elementary and secondary education in public and private schools.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TRANSFERRING THE POWERS OF THE PROVINCE TO ISSUE PERMITS AND IMPOSE TAXES ON SAND, GRAVEL AND OTHER QUARRY RESOURCES TO THE CITY OR MUNICIPALITY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF1991
rows.abstract: The permit to extract sand, gravel and other quarry resources, shall be issued exclusively by the city or municipal mayor pursuant to the ordinance of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.> The proceeds of the tax on sand, gravel and other quarry resourcesshall be distributed as follows: (1) Province - Thirty percent (30%); (2) Component City or Municipality where the sand, gravel and other Resources are extracted - Thirty percent (30%); and (3) Barangay where the sand, gravel and other quarry resources are extracted Forty percent (40%).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ALLOCATION FOR HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT FROM THE TWENTY PERCENT (20%) DEVELOPMENT FUND OF PROVINCES AND CITIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 287 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Each local government unit shall appropriate in its annual budget no less than twenty percent (20%) of its annual internal revenue allotment for development projects: PROVIDED, THAT TEN PERCENT OF SAID DEVELOPMENT FUND SHALL BE SET ASIDE BY PROVINCIAL AND CITY GOVERNMENTS FOR A SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM AT THE COLLEGIATE AND POST-GRADUATE LEVELS, PREFERABLY IN THE FIELDS OF MANAGEMENT, ECONOMICS, FINANCE, ENGINEERING, ARCHITECTURE, ELECTRONICS AND APPLIED SCIENCES, TO DESERVING RESIDENTS OF THE PROVINCE OR  CITY UNDER THE SUPERVISION AND DIRECTION OF A SCHOLARSHIP BOARD COMPOSED OF THE GOVERNOR OR CITY MAYOR AS CHAIRMAN, THE PROVINCIAL OR CITY SCHOOLS DIVISION SUPERINTENDENT AS VICE-CHAIRMAN, AND THE MEMBERS OF THE LOCAL SCHOOL BOARDS AS MEMBERSS, WITH ONE REPRESENTATIVE EACH FROM THE PRIVATE BUSINESS SECTOR NON-GOVERNMENTA L ORGANIZATIONS. Copies of the development plans for local government units shall be furnished the Department of Interior and Local Government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MORE EQUITABLE SHARE IN FAVOR OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS (LGUs) IN THE PROCEEDS FROM THE DEVELOPMENT AND UTILIZATION OF THE NATIONAL WEALTH, AMENDING SECTIONS 289, 290, 291 AND 293 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: "SEC. 289. Share in Proceeds from the Development and Utilization of the National Wealth. Local government units shall have an equitable share in the proceeds derived from the utilization and development of the national wealth within their respective areas, including sharing the same with the inhabitants by way of direct benefits. "NATIONAL WEALTH' SHALL BE DEFINED AS ALL. NATURAL RESOURCES SITUATED WITHIN THE PHILIPPINE TERRITORIAL JURISIDCTION INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO LANDS OF PUBLIC DOMAIN, WATERS, MINERALS, POTENTIALS ENERGY SOURCES, GAS AND OIL DEPOSITS, FOREST PRODUCTS, FLORA AND FAUNA, FISHERY AND AQUATIC RESOURCES, ALL QUARRY PRODUCTS, AND OTHER RESOURCES WHICH CAN BE EXTRACTED AND UTILIZED."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE TRANSFER OF ANCESTRAL LAND BELONGING TO THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLE TO NONMEMBERS, AMENDING SECTION 8 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8371, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "SEC. 8. Rights to Ancestral Lands. - The right of ownerhsip and possession of the ICCs/IPs to their ancestral lands shall be recognized and protected.  > a) Right to transfer land/property. - Such right shall include the right to transfer land or property rights to/among members of the same ICCs/IPs , subject to customary laws and traditions of the community concerned. ANY SALE, TRANSFER OR ENCUMBRANCE OF THE ANCESTRAL LAND MADE BY AN IP IN FAVOR OF NON-MEMBERS OF THE ICC CONCERNED SHALL BE VOID.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL MINORITIES since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-06-05, transmitted to on 2003-06-11 and received by the Senate on 2003-06-12
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING PERMANENT RESIDENCE STATUS UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS TO VIETNAMESE REFUGEES THROUGH A SOCIAL INTEGRATION PROGRAM
rows.abstract: Upon the effectivity of this Act, Vietnamese refugees who arrived in the Philippines as asylum seekers, betweeen January 1, 1989 to December 31, 1995, are hereby granted permanent residence status upon compliance with the requirement thereunder. Consequently, they shall not be prosecuted for crimes defined under Commonwealth Act No. 613, otherwise known as the Immigration Act of 1940.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05970

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING DULY ELECTED BARANGAY CHAIRPERSONS A MINIMUM MONTHLY COMPENSATION CORRESPONDING TO SALARY GRADE TEN (10) AS PRESCRIBED UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6758, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SALARY STANDARDIZATION LAW
rows.abstract: "Punong Barangay Compensation Act of 2001." Rationale: This bill is crafted in the premise that while Barangay Chairpersons, as heads of the country's basic political units, called the Barangay, play significant and critical roles in nation-building, the State somehow does not give in return the right and proper compensation due them.  It is noteworthy that among the other duties that they are accountable with is the enormous and innumerable responsibilitie s of maintaining the smooth, effective and efficient operations of their respective political units. They act as heads of the primary planning and implementing agencies of government programs, projects and activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE IMPOSITION OF AN IDLE LAND TAX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: There is hereby imposed an idle land tax to replace the local idle land tax authorized under the Local Government Code at the rate of five percent (5%) per annum based on the assessed value of the property as determined  by the Provincial or City Assessor of the Province or City where the property is located, or by the Municipal Assessor in the case of idle lands situated in the municipalities within Metropolitan Manila. The listing and assessment of idle lands shall be conducted and completedwithin six (6) months after the effectivity of this Act. The updating or reassessment shall coincide with the triennial general revision for real property tax purposes. Provided, that the tax thereon shall be collected on the first day of January folllowing the year it was assessed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF POLITICAL DYNASTIES
rows.abstract: The history of Philippine politics is said to be history of successive families or clans who had dominated and continue reigning in both local and national policis. Among the first serious steps taken by a politician once elected to public office isto build strong political base that will ensure not only his re-election but also that such electoral support will extend to his spouse or descendents or next-of-kin. The abuses and corruption spawned by this system of patronage characteristic of the old political order under martial law has also aggravated the peace and order problem by further feeling discontented among the rebels and their mass sympathizers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09174) enacted on 2002-11-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIX THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED SIXTY-EIGHT, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT INSTITUTING A BALIKBAYAN PROGRAM', BY PROVIDING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS AND PRIVILEGES TO BALIKBAYAN, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Some amendments proposed in this bill include: (1) Increase of current balikbayan purchase limit from US$1,000.00 to US$2,000.00; (2) Making the balikbayan shopping privilege available only at all government-owne d and-controlled duty free ships; (3) Extending the balikbayan shopping privilege from forty-eight (48) hours to seven (7) days; (4) Adding a tax-free purchase in the amount of US$2,000.00 or its equivalent in Philippine peso and other acceptable foreign currencies for the exclusive purchase of livelihood tools and equipment which can also be claimed by immediate family members even while the balikbayan is still abroad; (5) A new provision establishing a Balikbyan Program Council is added into the proposed bill; and (6) Allows thee balikbayan and OFWs to purchase goods in Philippine peso.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04534

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, ARTS AND NATIONAL HERITAGE DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to create the Department of Culture and National Heritage separate from the Department of Education, Culture and Sports (DECS). Under this Act, the bll provides police powers in the new Office which shall function and exercise extra-legal and quasi-judicial powers to prosecute criminal cases relative to violations of laws pertaining to the promotion, protection and preservation of culture and national heritage.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PARAGRAPH THREE, ARTICLE TWENTY-NINE OF ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-EIGHT HUNDRED FIFTEEN, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: "SECTION 1. Paragraph 3 of Article 29 of Act Numbered 3815, otherwise known as the Revised Penal Code as amended, is hereby amended to read as follows: 'Whenever an accused has undergone preventive suspensions for a period equal or more than the possible (maximum) MINIMUM imprisonment of the offense charge to which he may be sentenced and his case is not yet terminated, he shall be released immediately without prejudice to the continuation of the trial therefore or the preceding on appeal, if the same is under review; PROVIDED, HOWEVER, THAT IF THE ACCUSED IS ABSENT WITHOUT JUSTIFIABLE CAUSE AT ANY STAGE OF THE TRIAL, THE COURT MAY, ON MOTU PROPIO, ORDER THE REARREST OF THE MACCUSED; PROVIDED, FINALLY THAT, RECIDIVISTS, HABITUAL, DELINQUENNTS, EXCAPEES, AND PERSONS CHARGED WITH HEINOUS CRIMES ARE EXCLUDED FROM THE COVERAGE OF THIS ACT.' In case the maximum penalty to which the accised is destierro, he shall be released after thirty (30) days of preventive imprisonment."
